sentence: A 79-year-old man who, after a planned laparoscopic cholecystectomy converted due to anatomical difficulties, presented on the first postoperative day with an external biliary fistula due to environmental drainage.

In the imaging tests performed, some of them even repeated twice (ultrasound, CT, CT with pigtail drainage of the biloma, cMRI, diagnostic ERCP and subsequent ERCP with placement even of a 7 cm 10 F biliary stent), it was not possible to demonstrate the cause of the persistent biliary fistula, presenting the integrity of the intra- and extrahepatic bile duct, with anatomical and functional characteristics of normal appearance.
The output of the external biliary fistula, however, ranged between 200 and 400 cc. diaries.

The analysis showed an alanini aminotransferase of 109 U/l (7-40 U/l); aspartate aminotransferase 98 U/l (7-40 U/l); GGT of 120 U/l (7-40 U/l); alkaline phosphatase of 262 U/l (7-40 U/l); total bilirubin of 1.8 mg/dl (0.2-1.3 mg/dl).

Despite the internal biliary drainage of the main bile duct, the persistence of the external biliary fistula made us suspect that we were dealing with an aberrant duct, so it was decided to intervene 45 days after the initial cholecystectomy, requesting our collaboration intraoperatively in view of the difficulties encountered in the identification and interpretation of the findings of the surgical field in the biliary hilum.

Only intraoperatively, cholangiography through the nozzle of the juxtahilar biliary fistula demonstrated that the lesion originated in an aberrant duct of the independent right anterior sector (segments V-VIII), with no relation to the rest of the intrahepatic biliary tree. confirming the suspected diagnosis and enabling the treatment of the lesion through a transanastomotic tutored Roux-en-Y loop cholangiolojejunostomy using a silicone pediatric feeding catheter.
On the 7th postoperative day, a transcatheter cholangiography was performed with absolute normality of the anastomosis and absence of leaks, and the patient could be discharged.
The transanastomotic tutor was removed one month after surgery after a second cholangiographic control demonstrating the total integrity and functionality of the anastomosis performed.
In the annual check-ups the patient maintains complete normality of the analytical tests.
